content.text: Daifug? is the Japanese climbing game formerly often known as Dai Hinmin. Players shed singles or combinations by beating the previous play, then exchange cards between ranks in later deals.

Daifugō emerged in Japan in the 1970s and rapidly became one of the most widely played card games in the country. It belongs to the same family as Big Two (Chinese), President (Western), and Zheng Shangyou (Chinese).

Three to six players are typical; the game is usually played by 3 to 6, and up to 8 can take part (often with a single 53-card pack in Japan). With five or more players the full title hierarchy applies (Dai Fugō, Fugō, heimin, Hinmin, Dai Hinmin); with three or four only Fugō (winner) and Hinmin (loser) are used.
Deal entire deck evenly. Players with extra cards start at a slight disadvantage.

items.text: Daihinmin (Simple form): No revolution, no suit lock. Simpler ruleset for beginners.
5-Player Daifugō: 5 players with ranks: Daifugō (1st), Fugō (2nd), Heimin (3rd), Hinmin (4th), Daihinmin (5th). Full exchange hierarchy.
